MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY REPORT
[redacted location] Cancer Center
Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine

Patient: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Ordering Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Lung adenocarcinoma genetic profiling for treatment guidance

SPECIMEN TYPE
Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue

TEST PERFORMED
Combined FISH and Molecular Analysis - Rapid-Amplicon EGFR Pathway Panel

METHODOLOGY
Next-Generation Sequencing: Targeted amplicon-based sequencing of BRAF, KRAS, EGFR, NRAS genes performed on Illumina NextSeq platform. Custom bioinformatics pipeline utilized for alignment, variant calling, and annotation. Minimum variant allele frequency detection threshold: 5%.

Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH): Break apart probes used for ALK (2p23) and ROS1 (6q22) rearrangement assessment. A minimum of 50 tumor nuclei evaluated per probe set.

RESULTS SUMMARY

PATHOGENIC VARIANTS DETECTED:
1. BRAF c.1799T>A, p.(Val600Glu) - Allele Frequency: 15%
2. KRAS c.35G>T, p.(Gly12Val) - Allele Frequency: 19%

FISH ANALYSIS:
- ALK rearrangement: NEGATIVE (2-4 copies of intact ALK gene observed)
- ROS1 rearrangement: NEGATIVE

ADDITIONAL FINDINGS:
- EGFR: No pathogenic variants detected. Note: Low coverage for codons 854-875 limiting detection sensitivity in this region
- NRAS: No pathogenic variants detected
- Other BRAF regions: No additional therapeutic/prognostic variants identified

DETAILED RESULTS

Gene	Variant	Protein Change	Allele Frequency	Clinical Significance
BRAF	c.1799T>A	p.Val600Glu	15%	Pathogenic - Activating mutation
KRAS	c.35G>T	p.Gly12Val	19%	Pathogenic - Activating mutation
EGFR	No variants detected	-	-	See coverage limitation note
NRAS	No variants detected	-	-	-

COVERAGE ANALYSIS
All targeted regions achieved >500x coverage except EGFR codons 854-875 (average coverage 45x)

CLINICAL INTERPRETATION

BRAF V600E Mutation (15% AF):
The BRAF V600E mutation results in constitutive activation of the MAPK signaling pathway. In non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), this alteration may predict response to BRAF inhibitors, particularly when used in combination with MEK inhibitors. FDA-approved combination therapies include dabrafenib plus trametinib.

KRAS G12V Mutation (19% AF):
KRAS mutations are associated with primary resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors in NSCLC. The presence of this mutation suggests the patient is unlikely to benefit from EGFR-targeted therapies. KRAS G12V may also impact response to certain immunotherapy approaches.

ALK and ROS1 Status:
Negative FISH results indicate the patient is unlikely to benefit from ALK inhibitors (e.g., alectinib, crizotinib) or ROS1 inhibitors.

ASSAY LIMITATIONS
- This assay detects single nucleotide variants and small insertions/deletions in targeted regions only
- Large insertions, deletions, or complex rearrangements may not be detected by NGS component
- Low coverage in EGFR codons 854-875 may result in false-negative results for variants in this region
- Variants below 5% allele frequency may not be reliably detected

Electronically signed by:
[redacted name], MD, PhD
Board Certified in Molecular Genetic Pathology
